স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১) CURB-65 scoring system is related to
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
CURB-65 is a clinical scoring system used to assess the severity of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and to guide decisions regarding hospital admission and mortality risk.

CURB-65 components:

Letter Finding Score
C Confusion 1
U Urea >7 mmol/L 1
R Respiratory rate ≥30/min 1
B Blood pressure low (SBP <90 or DBP ≤60 mmHg) 1
65 Age ≥65 years 1

Higher scores indicate more severe pneumonia and increased mortality risk.

  • Asthma: Assessed by symptoms, peak flow, and exacerbation severity.

  • COPD: Uses tools like GOLD classification and exacerbation criteria.

  • Bronchiectasis: Assessed by severity scores such as FACED or BSI.

Exam Pearl:
CURB-65 → Severity assessment of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ২) Most common infecting agent in CAP
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The most common infecting agent in community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus).

Features:

  • Most common cause of typical CAP

  • Gram-positive, lancet-shaped diplococci

  • Causes lobar pneumonia with:

    • Fever

    • Productive cough

    • Pleuritic chest pain

    • Rust-coloured sputum (classically)

  • Staphylococcus aureus: Causes pneumonia, especially after influenza or in hospitalized patients, but is not the commonest CAP organism.

  • Mycoplasma pneumoniae: Common cause of atypical pneumonia, especially in young adults, but less common overall.

  • Legionella: Causes atypical pneumonia with systemic features (e.g., hyponatraemia, GI symptoms).

Exam Pearl:
Most common cause of CAP → Streptococcus pneumoniae.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৩) Type of hypersensitivity reaction in TB
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The hypersensitivity reaction in tuberculosis (TB) is Type IV (delayed-type) hypersensitivity.

Mechanism:

  • Mediated by T lymphocytes (cell-mediated immunity), especially Th1 cells.

  • Sensitized T cells release cytokines (e.g., IFN-γ) that activate macrophages.

  • This causes granuloma formation and tissue damage.

  • The Mantoux (tuberculin) skin test is an example of a delayed hypersensitivity reaction.

  • Anaphylactic: Type I hypersensitivity (IgE-mediated), seen in allergies and anaphylaxis.

  • Immune complex mediated: Type III hypersensitivity, seen in diseases like SLE and serum sickness.

  • Complement based: Not a classification of hypersensitivity reaction.

Exam Pearl:
TB → Type IV hypersensitivity → Delayed T-cell mediated reaction.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৪) Which anti-TB drug forms the cornerstone of 6-mlnths chemotherapy
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Rifampicin forms the cornerstone of the 6-month standard anti-tuberculosis (TB) chemotherapy regimen because it is the most important bactericidal and sterilizing drug in the regimen.

Standard 6-month regimen for drug-sensitive TB:

  • Intensive phase (2 months): HRZE

    • H = Isoniazid

    • R = Rifampicin

    • Z = Pyrazinamide

    • E = Ethambutol

  • Continuation phase (4 months): HR

    • Isoniazid + Rifampicin

Why Rifampicin is important:

  • Kills actively dividing and dormant organisms

  • Prevents relapse

  • Allows shorter treatment duration

  • Isoniazid: Most potent early bactericidal drug but not the cornerstone for shortening therapy.

  • Pyrazinamide: Essential for sterilizing activity in the intensive phase.

  • Ethambutol: Mainly prevents resistance.

Exam Pearl:
Cornerstone drug of 6-month TB chemotherapy → Rifampicin.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৫) Retrobulbar neuritis is a major adverse reaction observed in therapy with
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Retrobulbar neuritis (optic neuritis) is the major adverse effect of Ethambutol therapy.

Mechanism:

  • Ethambutol causes optic nerve toxicity by affecting mitochondrial function in retinal ganglion cells.

  • It leads to:

    • Reduced visual acuity

    • Loss of red–green colour discrimination

    • Central scotoma

Monitoring:

  • Baseline and periodic visual acuity and colour vision testing are recommended, especially with prolonged therapy or higher doses.

  • Isoniazid: Peripheral neuropathy (prevented by pyridoxine), hepatitis.

  • Pyrazinamide: Hepatotoxicity, hyperuricaemia, arthralgia.

  • Streptomycin: Ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.

Exam Pearl:
Ethambutol → Optic neuritis → Red-green colour blindness.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৬) Investigation of choice in Bronchiectasis
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The investigation of choice for diagnosing bronchiectasis is HRCT of the chest.

Why HRCT is preferred:

  • It provides detailed visualization of bronchial dilatation and airway changes.

  • Classic HRCT findings:

    • Bronchial dilatation (bronchus larger than accompanying pulmonary artery → signet ring sign)

    • Lack of bronchial tapering

    • Visible bronchi within 1 cm of pleural surface

  • CXR: May show suggestive features but has low sensitivity and cannot reliably confirm diagnosis.

  • MRI: Not routinely used for bronchiectasis evaluation.

  • USG: Not useful for assessing bronchial anatomy.

Exam Pearl:
Bronchiectasis diagnosis → HRCT chest (gold standard/investigation of choice).

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৭) Amber coloured pleural fluid indicates
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Amber-coloured pleural fluid is classically associated with tuberculous pleural effusion.

Features of TB pleural effusion:

  • Usually straw-coloured/amber fluid

  • Exudative effusion

  • Predominantly lymphocytic

  • High pleural fluid ADA (adenosine deaminase) level

  • CCF: Causes transudative pleural effusion, usually clear/straw-coloured, due to increased hydrostatic pressure.

  • Rheumatoid arthritis (RA): Pleural fluid may be low glucose with high LDH; can be turbid.

  • SLE: Can cause pleural effusion but amber colour is not a classic association.

Exam Pearl:
Amber/straw-coloured lymphocytic pleural effusion → Tuberculosis (TB).

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৮) Removal of more than ... L of pleural fluid at a time may risk re-expansion pulmonary injury?
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Removal of more than 1.5 litres of pleural fluid at a time may increase the risk of re-expansion pulmonary oedema (RPE), a potentially serious complication after rapid drainage of a large pleural effusion.

Mechanism:

  • Rapid re-expansion of a collapsed lung causes increased pulmonary capillary permeability → fluid leakage into lung tissue → pulmonary oedema.

Prevention:

  • Drain pleural fluid slowly

  • Avoid excessive negative pressure during drainage

  • Monitor symptoms such as cough, chest discomfort, and breathlessness

  • 0.1 L, 0.5 L, 1.0 L: Usually below the commonly cited risk threshold.

Exam Pearl:
Pleural fluid removal >1.5 L at once → Risk of re-expansion pulmonary oedema.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৯) The combination of absent breath sound and a resonant percussion note is a diagnostic of
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The combination of absent breath sounds with a resonant (hyper-resonant) percussion note is diagnostic of pneumothorax.

Mechanism:

  • Air enters the pleural space → lung collapses partially or completely.

  • Air in the pleural cavity prevents transmission of breath sounds → absent breath sounds.

  • Air produces a hollow sound on percussion → hyper-resonant note.

  • Pleurisy: Usually causes a pleural rub and may have normal breath sounds.

  • Pleural effusion: Causes reduced/absent breath sounds but dull percussion note due to fluid.

  • Empyema: Causes pleural fluid collection → stony dull percussion note.

Exam Pearl:
Absent breath sound + hyper-resonant percussion → Pneumothorax.
Absent breath sound + dull percussion → Pleural effusion.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১০) D-shaped shadow in CXR indicates
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
A D-shaped shadow on chest X-ray is classically seen in empyema, especially loculated pleural empyema.

Mechanism:

  • In empyema, pus collects in the pleural cavity.

  • When the fluid becomes loculated, it forms a characteristic lenticular (D-shaped) opacity on CXR.

  • The collection may appear as a localized pleural mass with obtuse angles to the chest wall.

  • Pleurisy: May show pleural thickening but not a typical D-shaped shadow.

  • Pleural effusion: Usually shows blunting of the costophrenic angle and a meniscus sign.

  • Pneumothorax: Shows increased radiolucency with absence of lung markings.

Exam Pearl:
D-shaped pleural opacity on CXR → Loculated empyema.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১১) COPD is diagnosed when post bronchodilator spirometry shows FEV/FVC is less than
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
COPD is diagnosed when post-bronchodilator spirometry shows FEV₁/FVC ratio < 70% (0.70).

Mechanism:

  • COPD causes persistent airflow limitation due to airway obstruction.

  • The obstruction is not fully reversible after bronchodilator use.

  • The key spirometric criterion is:

Post-bronchodilator FEV₁/FVC < 0.70 → Diagnostic of COPD

  • FEV₁: Indicates severity of airflow limitation.

  • FVC: Total forced vital capacity.

Other options:

  • 30%, 40%, 50%: These values may indicate severity in some contexts but are not diagnostic cut-offs.

Exam Pearl:
COPD diagnosis → Post-BD FEV₁/FVC < 70%.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১২) Symptoms of asthma worsens in the
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Symptoms of asthma commonly worsen in the early morning hours (especially around 2–6 AM) due to circadian variation in airway responsiveness.

Mechanism:

  • Increased vagal tone at night → bronchoconstriction

  • Reduced endogenous cortisol levels → increased airway inflammation

  • Increased airway hyper-responsiveness during sleep

Typical nocturnal asthma symptoms:

  • Cough (especially at night/early morning)

  • Wheezing

  • Chest tightness

  • Shortness of breath

  • Midday: Symptoms are usually less prominent.

  • Evening/Early night: Symptoms may occur but are less characteristic than early morning worsening.

Exam Pearl:
Asthma symptoms worsen → Early morning (nocturnal/early morning asthma).

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৩) Which drug is added in initial add-on therapy step of management of asthma
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
In asthma management, the initial add-on therapy for patients whose symptoms are not controlled on low-dose inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) is the addition of an inhaled LABA.

Stepwise asthma management:

  • Step 1: As-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol (or equivalent)

  • Step 2: Low-dose ICS

  • Step 3 (initial add-on therapy): Add LABA to low-dose ICS → ICS/LABA combination

Why LABA:

  • Produces prolonged bronchodilation

  • Improves symptom control and lung function

  • Reduces exacerbations when combined with ICS

  • Low-dose ICS: It is the initial controller therapy, not an add-on.

  • LTRA (e.g., montelukast): Alternative add-on, especially in allergic rhinitis or aspirin-sensitive asthma.

  • LAMA (e.g., tiotropium): Usually added in more severe asthma not controlled with ICS/LABA.

Exam Pearl:
Asthma uncontrolled on low-dose ICS → Add inhaled LABA first.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৪) Feature suggesting near-fatal asthma
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
A raised PaCO₂ is a key feature suggesting near-fatal asthma.

In severe asthma:

  • Initially, patients hyperventilate → PaCO₂ falls (respiratory alkalosis).

  • As airway obstruction worsens and respiratory muscles become exhausted, ventilation fails → PaCO₂ rises.

  • A normal or raised PaCO₂ in a severely breathless asthma patient is a warning sign of impending respiratory failure.

Other features:

  • Silent chest: Indicates very severe airflow obstruction and may be seen in near-fatal asthma.

  • Cyanosis: Suggests severe hypoxaemia but is a later sign.

  • Exhaustion: Indicates respiratory muscle fatigue and impending failure.

Exam Pearl:
Severe asthma + rising PaCO₂ → near-fatal asthma (impending respiratory failure).

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৫) Antimicrobials causing pulmonary eosinophilia except
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Pulmonary eosinophilia is a drug-induced lung reaction characterized by eosinophilic infiltration of lung tissue, often presenting with cough, fever, dyspnoea, and pulmonary infiltrates.

Common antimicrobial causes:

  • Nitrofurantoin ✅ (classic cause of acute/chronic pulmonary eosinophilia)

  • Tetracycline ✅

  • Penicillin ✅ (can cause allergic pulmonary reactions)

Erythromycin is not a typical cause of pulmonary eosinophilia.

Exam Pearl:
Drug-induced pulmonary eosinophilia → Nitrofurantoin is a classic antimicrobial cause.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৬) Causes of chronic type-2 respiratory failure excludes
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Chronic type-2 respiratory failure is characterized by:

  • ↑ PaCO₂ (hypercapnia)

  • Often associated with hypoxaemia

  • Due to chronic alveolar hypoventilation

Common causes include:

  • COPD ✅ (most common cause)

  • Obstructive sleep apnoea ✅

  • Neuromuscular disorders/myopathies ✅ (respiratory muscle weakness causing hypoventilation)

Lobar collapse (atelectasis) is usually an acute/subacute cause of hypoxaemic respiratory failure (Type 1) due to ventilation–perfusion mismatch, not a typical cause of chronic type-2 respiratory failure.

Exam Pearl:
Chronic Type-2 respiratory failure → COPD, obesity/sleep apnoea, neuromuscular weakness.
Lobar collapse → usually Type-1 respiratory failure.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৭) Most common cell type of lung cancer
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The most common cell type of lung cancer overall is adenocarcinoma.

Key points:

  • Adenocarcinoma is now the most common type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

  • It is commonly found in:

    • Peripheral areas of the lung

    • Non-smokers and females more frequently than other types

  • It often involves mutations such as EGFR, ALK, and KRAS.

  • Squamous cell carcinoma: Historically the most common, strongly associated with smoking, usually central/hilar location.

  • Small-cell lung carcinoma: Highly aggressive, associated with smoking, causes paraneoplastic syndromes, but less common.

  • Large-cell carcinoma: Rare subtype of NSCLC.

Exam Pearl:
Most common lung cancer type → Adenocarcinoma.
Most common lung cancer associated with smoking → Squamous cell carcinoma (classic teaching).

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৮) Non metastatic extra pulmonary effect that is usually associated with small-cell lung cancer
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The most common non-metastatic extrapulmonary (paraneoplastic) effect associated with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is SIADH.

Mechanism:

  • Small-cell lung carcinoma arises from neuroendocrine cells.

  • It can produce ectopic ADH, causing:

    • Water retention

    • Dilutional hyponatraemia

    • Low serum osmolality

    • Inappropriately concentrated urine

Other paraneoplastic syndromes of SCLC:

  • Ectopic ACTH production → Cushing syndrome

  • Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome

Options:

  • Carcinoid syndrome: More associated with carcinoid tumours (neuroendocrine tumours), not typical SCLC.

  • Gynaecomastia: Not a classic SCLC association.

  • Hypercalcaemia: Classically associated with squamous cell carcinoma due to PTHrP production.

Exam Pearl:
Small-cell lung cancer → SIADH + Ectopic ACTH + Lambert-Eaton syndrome.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৯) The most frequent symptom of respiratory disease
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The most frequent symptom of respiratory disease is cough.

Why cough is common:

  • It is a protective reflex that helps clear secretions, foreign particles, and irritants from the respiratory tract.

  • It occurs in many respiratory conditions, including:

    • Upper respiratory tract infections

    • Asthma

    • COPD

    • Pneumonia

    • Bronchiectasis

    • Lung cancer

    • TB

Other options:

  • Chest pain: May occur in pleurisy, pneumonia, pulmonary embolism, etc., but is less frequent.

  • Breathlessness (dyspnoea): A common symptom but usually indicates more significant airway or parenchymal involvement.

  • Haemoptysis: Important but occurs less commonly.

Exam Pearl:
Most common respiratory symptom → Cough.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ২০) Which disease occurs less frequently in smokers
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Sarcoidosis occurs less frequently in smokers. Smoking has been observed to have an inverse association with sarcoidosis, although the exact mechanism is not fully understood.

Associations with smoking:

  • COPD: Strongly associated with cigarette smoking ✅

  • Lung cancer: Major risk factor is smoking ✅

  • Myocardial infarction (MI): Smoking is a major cardiovascular risk factor ✅

  • Sarcoidosis: Less common among smokers ✅

Exam Pearl:
Smoking increases COPD, lung cancer, and MI risk — but sarcoidosis is less frequent in smokers.
